tagline: Upriver, beside the water that was once the highway.
intro: From Mineralwells at the I-77 end, the two-lane road follows the Little Kanawha upstream for about 77 miles, through Elizabeth, Grantsville and Glenville to Burnsville near I-79. The river meanders and the road keeps with it nearly the whole way, past farmland, forest and small rural towns.

Before the road the river was the highway. Barrels of oil went down it to Parkersburg, and at Glenville, where the paper first printed "The West Virginia Hills" in 1885, river traffic ran the town until road building helped end the riverboats by the late 1930s.

moments.title: Burning Springs
moments.text: Oil was sold here for lamps years before Drake's well in Pennsylvania, and in May 1863 Confederate raiders set every well afire, so that the river burned for miles.

moments.title: Duck Run Cable Suspension Bridge
moments.text: At Trubada a swinging bridge built in 1922 hangs 351 feet across the river on two wire rope cables strung between four concrete towers.

moments.title: Burnsville Bridge
moments.text: Near the end of the run, an 1893 truss from a Cleveland iron works crosses the Little Kanawha on two stone piers.
